newsitem.title: USA: U.S., EU discuss aviation subsidy agreement.
newsitem.headline: U.S., EU discuss aviation subsidy agreement.

text.p: U.S. and European Union officials on Thursday held the first of two days of talks on a 1992 transatlantic agreement that limits direct and indirect subsidies to civil aviation industries.
Officials from both sides said they spent Thursday afternoon going over technical issues. Talks are set to continue Friday morning.
Both sides said the talks were regularly scheduled under the 1992 agreement and unrelated to the proposed merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas, which is now nearing an important EU vote.
EU chief trade negotiator Peter Carl is leading the European delegation, while Joe Papovich, acting assistant U.S. trade representative for industry, is leading the U.S. side in the talks.
European Union Trade Commissioner Leon Brittan has said Europe was unhappy with the way the United States was implementing the trade agreement.
